original_question: Only three noncommutative digital signature schemes were known at the time of writing; can additional noncommutative digital signature schemes be designed?
target_in_paper: Section 11, Open Problems, General problem 7: So far there are three known non-commutative digital signatures have been designed, can we design more non-commutative digital signatures? ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1103.4093))
correct_elements: Your draft is already very close to the paper's exact target: it preserves the specific design question, the non-commutative setting, and the premise that only three such signatures were known at the time of the survey. It also stays on the right problem rather than drifting to the neighboring questions about provable security, public-key exchange, or authentication. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1103.4093))
missing_details: The paper states this specifically as Section 11, Open Problems, General problem 7, so the target is an open design problem, not a theorem, conjecture, or security claim. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1103.4093))

In the nearby formal context of Section 6, a digital signature scheme is understood in the public-key sense: it consists of key-generation, signing, and verification algorithms, each described as probabilistic polynomial-time, with intended security against probabilistic polynomial-time forgery. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1103.4093))

The scope is non-commutative cryptography broadly, not only group-based cryptography: Section 6 gives a nonabelian-group signature example and also mentions a semiring-based example outside group theory. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1103.4093))

The open problem itself does not impose a specific platform group, algebra, hardness assumption, or proof-of-security requirement; those are handled separately by nearby open problems on platform choice, protocol analysis, and provable security. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1103.4093))
The phrase "so far" is relative to the survey's 2011 time frame, and the item itself does not enumerate the three known constructions by name. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/abs/1103.4093))

No ambient field, degree restriction, homogeneity condition, nilpotency assumption, or similar formula-level hypotheses are part of this particular problem; it is a schematic cryptographic design question. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1103.4093))
refined_question: As of the 2011 survey on noncommutative algebraic cryptography, only three non-commutative digital signatures were known. Can one construct further non-commutative public-key digital signature schemes on non-commutative algebraic platforms, in the Section 6 sense of probabilistic polynomial-time key-generation, signing, and verification algorithms, beyond those three? ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/abs/1103.4093))
justification: This is the nearest official formulation in the paper: the draft clearly targets the Section 11 open-problem list, specifically General problem 7, rather than any broader neighboring issue. To make the question stand alone without broadening it, the only necessary nearby context is Section 6's definition of a digital signature scheme and its examples, which show that the paper's scope is non-commutative platforms generally rather than only nonabelian groups. The rewrite therefore keeps the paper's exact design objective, adds only the public-key signature-scheme framework that the paper explicitly supplies, and avoids importing the separate open problems about provable security, authentication schemes, or platform-group selection. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1103.4093))
